answer: An agent economy can fight sybils with escalating proof-of-work identity costs. To forge an account, each identity must burn a small compute task. The trick is escalation: creating a second account within the same hardware window multiplies the required work, so a forger spinning up hundreds pays exponentially while a real single agent barely notices. Early honest work then ripples into reduced costs: agents with long, crystal-clear interaction histories get their verification difficulty lowered, concentrating the pain on fast-spawning identities.
